execution.allocation: No stored replicate panels, covariance matrices, resample matrices, or massive loops. <=2400 panels, each two 28x132 lists, plus O(132) counters; variance uses O(days) AR recurrence. Serialized protocol/result each <=8 MiB.
execution.budget_failure: Check monotonic deadline each replicate. On deadline, SIGTERM, or exception, persist partial honest RUNTIME_OR_EXECUTION_FAILURE with nonzero exit; no tuning/retry selection.
execution.scope: Synthetic only; no data acquisition, reserved observations, returns/profitability claims, production integration, or changes to old results/frozen future protocol. Walkforward NOT_READY/NOT_RUN.

failure_hypothesis_and_change: The original saved result remains FAIL: marginal medians .1083/.0917/.1167/.1604 and 14 sparse invalid families. This redesign does not explain that failure away.

Old bootstrap compares an observed event ratio to ratios from sample-mean-centered overlapping nonwrapping blocks. This is not a finite-sample pivotal/exchangeable null distribution. Estimated centering, random denominators, edge weights and effective block count (~28/5) can distort tails even under iid dates.

Five-day moving-block consistency requires suitable weak dependence/mixing, increasing block length with block length / sample size tending to zero, sufficient moments, and stable denominators. Twenty-eight dates with block length five gives no exact guarantee; AR1 dependence crosses block boundaries.

Assigning zero to an empty bootstrap ratio invents a statistic; missing original cells cannot become evidence. B=199 has floor .005, above .0003788, so zero Holm rejections were structurally uninformative.
Change to one exact synthetic Gaussian oracle, NOT a practical replacement estimator. Known covariance removes centering/bootstrap mismatch and is a mathematical reference benchmark only.

monte_carlo_and_gate.budget_power: 600 planned families/scenario <2000 required; family Monte Carlo precision is intentionally insufficient for PASS, even with zero rejections. Resolution of analytic p-values is not Monte Carlo calibration power.
monte_carlo_and_gate.fail: Any marginal lower Wilson bound > .075 or complete-family lower bound > .075 gives FAIL. Intervals describe simulation uncertainty, not market uncertainty.
monte_carlo_and_gate.intervals: Two-sided 95% Wilson per cell and per complete-family any-rejection indicator. Per-cell intervals are pointwise, not simultaneous; no pooled-cell binomial interval.
monte_carlo_and_gate.missing: Any incomplete family is REFUSED. If any replicate is refused, no unconditional FWER estimate/interval or PASS; do not silently condition FWER on complete families.
monte_carlo_and_gate.overall: FAIL if any in-scope scenario fails; otherwise INCONCLUSIVE unless every scenario passes. Mismatch diagnostic cannot validate the oracle or markets.
monte_carlo_and_gate.pass: Only if no refusals, every upper Wilson bound <=.075, >=2000 independent families, family interval width<=.02, and assumptions apply. Otherwise INCONCLUSIVE.
monte_carlo_and_gate.unit: One independently generated whole 132-cell panel per replicate; 132 correlated cells never multiply Monte Carlo N. Marginal Wilson intervals use each cell's available independent replicate count.

predeclared_mismatch_diagnostic: For AR1 only, also compute the same oracle formula with deliberately false K=I. Report INCONCLUSIVE_ASSUMPTIONS_VIOLATED regardless of its observed rates; FAIL if any marginal Wilson lower bound exceeds .075. Never select between methods using results.

preserved_scenarios.ar1_day_null: a=.55, b=.35, noise=.75; global rho=.65, arm rho=.45, both initialized at zero before first innovation, as in old generator.
preserved_scenarios.counts: Each active cell/date has 1+Bernoulli(.35)+Bernoulli(.10) events; Gaussian factors shared by events on a day; independent event noise.
preserved_scenarios.iid_day_null: a=.55, b=.35, noise=.75; independent Gaussian days.
preserved_scenarios.shared_crossarm_factor: a=.90, b=.20, noise=.25; independent days, strong global dependence.
preserved_scenarios.sparse_empty_days: a=.65, b=.25, noise=.70; independent days; shared date activity .35 and conditional cell activity .55. Empty families are possible and must be refused.

assumptions: Gaussian zero-mean factors and event errors with exactly known model loadings, innovation variances, AR coefficients and initialization.
Activity masks and counts are independent of all Gaussian outcomes; condition on them when computing variance.
IID scenarios have independent UTC-day vectors. AR1 is NOT day independent and is calibrated only with its known temporal covariance.
No market validity from Gaussianity, estimated covariance, marginal symmetry, or independent-day sign flips is asserted.
single_design.cross_cell_dependence: One shared global Gaussian trajectory and eleven arm trajectories, with independent Gaussian noise per event. Whole panels are generated together; no independent simulation of individual hypothesis tests. Holm needs marginal superuniformity, not independent cells.
single_design.empty_days: Retain all 28 calendar rows. Count zero requires sum zero. A completely empty cell has no statistic/p-value, not Z=0; refuse the entire fixed Holm family without dropping cells.

finite_resolution.if_simulation_p_values_were_used: At least 2640 random draws would be required for 1/(B+1)<=0.05/132; they are not used in this design.

single_design.known_variance: V_j = a^2 c_j' K_global c_j + b^2 c_j' K_arm c_j + noise^2 sum(c_j). K=I for independent dates. For zero-initialized AR1, K[t,u]=rho^abs(t-u)*(1-rho^(2*(min(t,u)+1))), with zero-based dates.
single_design.null: All 132 event means are zero in the specified synthetic Gaussian factor model, conditional on the exogenous event counts/activity mask.
single_design.p_value: One-sided analytic Gaussian survival probability erfc(Z/sqrt(2))/2. No bootstrap, signs, fitted covariance, or simulation-ranked p-values.
single_design.statistic: Z_j = sum_d daily_sum[d,j] / sqrt(V_j); equivalently the event-weighted mean divided by its KNOWN conditional standard deviation.
